questions.knowledge_point: Completing the Square on a Quadratic Expression
questions.problem: Complete the square on the quadratic expression ${x}^{2}+10x+16.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the coefficient of the linear term as a product with $2$ as a factor:

$$
{x}^{2}+2\cdot 5x+16
$$

Now, here's the trick. We *add* and *then subtract* ${5}^{2},$ writing the constant term $16$ last:

$$
{{x}^{2}+2\cdot 5x+{5}^{2}}_{⏟}-\,{5}^{2}+16
$$

The first three terms form a perfect square, which we factor as follows:

$$
(x+5{)}^{2}-{5}^{2}+16
$$

Finally, evaluating the last two terms, we get

$$
(x+5{)}^{2}-9.
$$

questions.problem: Complete the square on the quadratic expression ${y}^{2}-4y+10.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the coefficient of the linear term as a product with $2$ as a factor:

$$
{y}^{2}-2\cdot 2y+10
$$

Now, here's the trick. We *add* and *then subtract* ${2}^{2},$ writing the constant term $10$ last:

$$
{{y}^{2}-2\cdot 2y+{2}^{2}}_{⏟}-\,{2}^{2}+10
$$

The first three terms form a perfect square, which we factor as follows:

$$
(y-2{)}^{2}-{2}^{2}+10
$$

Finally, evaluating the last two terms, we get

$$
(y-2{)}^{2}+6.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Completing the Square When the Perfect Square is Isolated: Negative Linear Term
questions.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{x}^{2}-2ax+{a}^{2}=(x-a{)}^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-8x+16 & = \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 4x+{4}^{2} & = \\ (x-4{)}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}-8x+16)+5 & = \\ (x-4{)}^{2}+5 & .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
If the expression ${x}^{2}-10x$ is written as $(x-p{)}^{2}+q$, then what are the values of $p$ and $q?$

$p=$
{{field-1}},
$\,q=$
{{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the coefficient of the linear term as a product with $2$ as a factor:

$$
{x}^{2}-2\cdot 5x+0
$$

Now, here's the trick. We *add* and *then subtract* ${5}^{2},$ writing the constant term $0$ last:

$$
{{x}^{2}-2\cdot 5x+{5}^{2}}_{⏟}-\,{5}^{2}+0
$$

The first three terms form a perfect square, which we factor as follows:

$$
(x-5{)}^{2}-{5}^{2}+0
$$

Finally, evaluating the last two terms, we get

$$
(x-5{)}^{2}-25
$$

Therefore, $p=5$ and $q=-25.$
